extraction.name: POPE
extraction.description: A polling-based object probing evaluation dataset/pipeline for evaluating object hallucination in large vision-language models using image-question-answer triples with Yes/No answers.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, and Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.citeAs: Li, Yifan, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, and Ji-Rong Wen. 2023. "Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models." arXiv:2305.10355.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: POPE is constructed from image caption datasets by obtaining ground-truth objects from human annotations or automatic segmentation, then creating Yes/No polling questions using ground-truth and sampled nonexistent objects under random, popular, and adversarial sampling strategies.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Input images and object annotations from image caption datasets such as MSCOCO, with objects also obtainable from automatic segmentation tools like SEEM.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Objects in each image are obtained from annotations or automatic segmentation; the ratio between ground-truth and nonexistent objects is set to 1:1; for MSCOCO evaluation, 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects are randomly selected and 6 questions are constructed per image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions with answer Yes are built from ground-truth objects, while questions with answer No are built by sampling nonexistent objects using random, popular, or adversarial sampling strategies; objects can come from human annotations or automatic segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzes consistency between POPE Yes/No responses and generated captions, finding strong correlation between objects mentioned in captions and Yes responses.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Object hallucination can hinder safe real-world deployment of LVLMs and may cause serious safety issues, such as wrong decisions in autonomous driving.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The visual instruction datasets used to build LVLMs have unbalanced object distributions, and LVLMs are prone to hallucinate frequently appearing objects and objects that frequently co-occur with ground-truth objects.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation only focuses on object hallucination rather than overall LVLM capability; results are based on subsets of validation sets due to computation limits; matching-based Yes/No detection can be inaccurate; automatic segmentation labels may differ from human annotations; and only a small number of LVLMs were compared.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of object hallucination in large vision-language models; can be used on annotated datasets and extended to unannotated datasets with automatic segmentation.

name.evidence: Besides, we further design a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation of object hallucination.

description.evidence: Given an image caption dataset, POPE focuses on constructing a set of triples, each of which consists of an image, multiple questions and their answers (“Yes” or “No”).

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: For example, due to an incorrect understanding of the extemal environment, an autonomous driving system would make wrong decisions when encountering unexpected events, which might lead to serious safety issues.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Therefore, we hypothesize that (1) LVLMs are prone to hallucinate frequently appearing objects in the visual instruction datasets; (2) LVLMs are prone to hallucinate objects that frequently co-occur with ground-truth objects in the image.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: First, we only focus on the object hallucination problem in LVLMs, while do not consider other aspects that can reflect the capacities of LVLMs.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: In this section, we devise Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation (POPE), a simple yet effective approach for evaluating hallucination in LVLMs.
